articles.title: Which coding-agent CLI is best for headless workflow automation?
articles.summary: A coding-agent CLI can feel quick in a terminal and still be expensive when a workflow starts it in a fresh container for every job. We measured that cost for six CLIs: start-up, time per turn, memory, image size and tokens. On overhead per job, pi was the lightest overall. Our own CLI, aictrl , won no metric but came second on four: session time, harness time per turn, memory and image size. Overhead is half the answer: this experiment does not measure whether an agent completes the task, which our next run will. articles.title: Context Mode – An Open-Source MCP Server That Reduces AI Coding Context Usage
articles.summary: Context window optimization for AI coding agents. Sandboxes tool output (98% reduction), persists session memory, and enforces routing across 17 platforms via MCP + hooks. Every MCP tool call dumps raw data into your context window. A Playwright snapshot costs 56 KB. Twenty GitHub issues cost 59 KB. One access log — 45 KB. After 30 minutes, 40% of your context is gone. And when the agent compacts the conversation to free space, it forgets which files it was editing, what tasks are in progress, and what you last asked for. articles.title: Will Agent Resource Registries ever have their moment, the way AI gateways did?
articles.summary: ARD is an open discovery protocol for agentic resources ( GitHub ). It allows an AI client to ask: "What is available for this task?" and lets a discovery service answer with matching resources. ARD sits entirely before invocation. It helps the client find the right resource; the resource is then invoked through its own native mechanism. An agentic resource is any external capability an AI client can call on to do a task — an agent, MCP server, Skill, Canvas, Plugin, API, or workflow — anything that can be described as an ARD entry . articles.title: QwenPU: An LLM running inside another LLM's weights
articles.summary: QwenPU is Qwen3.5-4B with a 32-bit RISC-V CPU and a vector unit compiled into its weights. The vector unit runs a whole neural network inside the model's forward passes: Andrej Karpathy's stories260K , the 260K-parameter Llama from llama2.c , runs as a program on it and writes its stories. It's part of Qwenputer : the same CPU, compiled into transformer layers in front of Qwen's own, every weight set by a compiler, with Qwen3.5's Gated DeltaNet state as its memory.
